analysis:
The supplied changes are a ProviderCore.version bump from 0.10.3 to 0.10.4 (ProviderCore.swift line 8) and release-runbook edits in docs/operations/provider-release.md (about lines 26-126). The runbook edits add the 0.10.4 preparation text, the pre-tag checks on submodule pins and metallib hash, the rollout ordering against platform PRs #516, #491 and #541, and an evidence table.

No executable security logic changed. The version bump is consumed by CLI output, registration and packaging, and scripts/check-release-version.sh enforces that the tag, source and built binary agree. It does not touch attestation, key handling, authorization, encryption or the hold socket.

The doc text describes feature behavior in the 0.10.4 changelog (Qwen JSON response_format, forced tool_choice, add-on hold, re-registration of unauthorized connections, a 30 s reconnect timeout). The changes that implement it are outside this batch, so I could not verify them. Relevant threat models are TB-011/T-053 (re-registration of unauthorized connections), TB-012/T-059 (add-on hold, with the coordinator side said to be in production via platform#514) and TB-002.

The runbook keeps release authorization and pipeline controls: human approval, signed tag, exact CodeDirectory registration, permanent revocation and no environment bypass. Nothing there weakens them. It states that no provider-version floor is needed because forced tool_choice goes only to providers that advertise it. That relies on external platform behavior (registry/tool_constraints.go) which I cannot see, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

The doc describes a rollout window in which a provider and coordinator disagree on Qwen JSON rendering. That produces cache-receipt mismatches and temporary cache-affinity quarantine. It affects availability and cache routing only, and the doc says serving is unaffected. It does not break confidentiality.

For integration: the code implementing the 0.10.4 behaviors (re-registration, hold socket, cache delta checkpoints) should be reviewed in its own source units.
